clues.q: Singer Norah Jones is the daughter of this sitar legend, who performed at Woodstock in 1969.
This playback singer, the younger sister of Lata Mangeshkar, recorded hits like “Dum Maro Dum” and “Piya Tu Ab To Aaja.”
Which Pakistani “Sufi rock” band, founded by guitarist Salman Ahmad, released the hit “Sayonee” in 1997?
Pandit Shivkumar Sharma brought this trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer into the world of Indian classical music.
Honored in Nepal as “Swar Samrat,” or emperor of voice, this singer recorded hundreds of beloved modern Nepali songs.
Often shortened to “K3G,” this 2001 Karan Johar family drama starred Shah Rukh Khan, Kajol, Hrithik Roshan and Kareena Kapoor.
clues.a: What is Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham?

clues.q: This Pakistani filmmaker won Academy Awards for the documentary shorts “Saving Face” and “A Girl in the River.”
Crowned Miss World in 1994, this actress played Paro in the 2002 film “Devdas.”
Sanam Saeed played Kashaf and Fawad Khan played Zaroon in this 2012–2013 Hum TV drama serial.
This Bangladeshi novelist, creator of the characters Himu and Misir Ali, also directed the 1994 film “Aguner Poroshmoni.”
Patanjali’s Sutras systematized this ancient practice of postures, breathing and meditation.
The Buddha is said to have given his first sermon at a deer park in this place near Varanasi.
Near present-day Islamabad, this UNESCO-listed ancient city was a great center of learning in the Gandhara region.
Under Rajaraja I, this Tamil dynasty built the towering Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur.
Written in Pali, this “Great Chronicle” of Sri Lanka recounts the island’s history beginning with the arrival of Prince Vijaya.
India celebrates Republic Day on January 26 because this founding document took effect on that date in 1950.
clues.a: What is the Constitution of India?

clues.q: In 1947, this politician became Pakistan’s first prime minister.
Honoring Bangladesh’s 1952 Language Movement, UNESCO proclaimed February 21 as this international observance.
clues.a: What is International Mother Language Day?

clues.q: In 1919, Afghanistan gained full control of its foreign affairs from Britain under this reforming ruler, who later took the title of king.
In 1994, this daughter of Sirimavo Bandaranaike became Sri Lanka’s first female president.
Brides across South Asia have intricate designs painted on their hands with a paste made from this plant.
Pakistan’s national dress pairs a long tunic with loose, pleated trousers; name the outfit.
Belted at the waist and worn to the knee, this robe is the national dress for men in Bhutan.
UNESCO recognized the traditional art of weaving this fine, patterned muslin sari of Bangladesh in 2013.
Prized for heavy silk and gold zari borders, these saris are woven in a Tamil Nadu temple town that was once the Pallava capital.
These triangular fried pastries are usually stuffed with spiced potatoes and peas.
This winter dessert is made by slow-cooking grated carrots with milk, sugar and ghee.
Made for Tihar and Dashain, this ring-shaped, deep-fried Nepali bread uses a sweet rice-flour batter.
This Sri Lankan dish of rice cooked in coconut milk is cut into diamond shapes and traditionally eaten on New Year’s morning.
The Bangladeshi town of Bogura is famous for this sweet, caramel-colored dairy dessert set in clay pots.

questions.q: Sport played on horseback with mallets?
Flute-playing Hindu god often shown with blue skin?
South Asian stew of spiced lentils?
Spiced milk tea sold at street stalls?
Mountain range along Nepal’s northern border?

clues.q: This Pakistani singer performed the 2022 Coke Studio smash “Pasoori” with Shae Gill.
clues.hint: His first name is shared with the fourth caliph.

clues.q: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is the best-known master of this side-blown bamboo flute.
clues.hint: Krishna is often pictured playing one.

clues.q: Legend says this musician in Emperor Akbar’s court could bring rain or light lamps with his ragas.
clues.hint: One of Akbar’s “Nine Jewels.”

clues.q: Which composer belongs to the “Trinity” of Carnatic music along with Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri?
clues.hint: He lived in Thiruvaiyaru, devoted to Rama.

clues.q: Lalon Shah is the most revered poet-singer of this mystic minstrel tradition of Bengal, recognized by UNESCO.
clues.hint: A four-letter name for wandering singers with ektaras.

clues.q: Nicknamed “King Khan,” this actor starred in “Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge” and “Pathaan.”
clues.hint: Fans often call him by his initials, SRK.

clues.q: Amitabh Bachchan became the face of this Indian version of “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?”
clues.hint: Often abbreviated KBC.

clues.q: Starring Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan, this 2022 Pakistani action film reimagined a 1979 Punjabi classic.
clues.a: What is The Legend of Maula Jatt?
clues.hint: Its villain is Noori Natt.

clues.q: This Sri Lankan actress is widely called the “Queen of Sinhala Cinema.”
clues.hint: She starred in Lester James Peries’s “Nidhanaya.”

clues.q: In 1983, this costume designer became the first Indian to win an Academy Award, for Richard Attenborough’s “Gandhi.”
clues.hint: Her first name means “sun.”

clues.q: Excavated in the 1920s in Punjab, Pakistan, this site gave its name to the Indus Valley Civilization’s alternate name.
clues.hint: It lies near the Ravi River, close to Sahiwal.

clues.q: This network of ancient trade routes linked China with Central Asia, passing through Afghanistan.
clues.hint: Named after a luxurious fabric.

clues.q: According to tradition, this son of Emperor Ashoka brought Buddhism to Sri Lanka.
clues.hint: His sister Sanghamitta is said to have followed him.

clues.q: From roughly the 4th to the 9th century CE, this dynasty ruled Nepal’s Kathmandu Valley.
clues.hint: It succeeded the Kirata rulers.

clues.q: Two colossal standing Buddhas were carved into the cliffs of this central Afghan valley around the 6th century.
clues.hint: A Silk Road valley in the Hindu Kush.

clues.q: This Albanian-born nun, who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, won the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize.
clues.hint: She was canonized in 2016.

clues.q: This Pakistani humanitarian, who built a vast volunteer ambulance network, received a state funeral in 2016.
clues.hint: His foundation bears his surname.

clues.q: This captain led Sri Lanka to victory over Australia in the 1996 Cricket World Cup final in Lahore.
clues.hint: His first name comes from a Mahabharata archer.

clues.q: This leader served as president of the Maldives from 1978 to 2008.
clues.hint: He studied at Al-Azhar University in Cairo.

clues.q: In 2008, this son of the Fourth King was crowned Bhutan’s fifth Dragon King.
clues.a: Who is Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck?
clues.hint: Educated at Oxford; married Queen Jetsun Pema.

clues.q: This Indian-born NASA astronaut first flew aboard Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997.
clues.hint: She grew up in Karnal, Haryana.

clues.q: This self-taught mathematician worked with G. H. Hardy at Cambridge and is the subject of “The Man Who Knew Infinity.”
clues.hint: The taxicab number 1729 is linked to him.

clues.q: This physicist won the 1930 Nobel Prize for discovering how light scatters, an effect now named for him.
clues.hint: India’s National Science Day honors his discovery.

clues.q: Born in Dhaka, this structural engineer designed Chicago’s Sears Tower and John Hancock Center.
clues.hint: Pioneer of the “tube” structural system.

clues.q: This Lahore-born astrophysicist shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics and gave his name to the maximum mass of a white dwarf.
clues.hint: NASA named an X-ray observatory after him.

clues.q: This Mughal emperor built the red-sandstone city of Fatehpur Sikri.
clues.hint: Often called “the Great.”

clues.q: Each Independence Day, India’s prime minister raises the flag at this Mughal fortress in Delhi.
clues.hint: Named for the color of its sandstone walls.

clues.q: Designed by Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay, this Islamabad mosque is shaped like a desert tent.
clues.hint: Named after a Saudi king.

clues.q: Bangladesh’s National Parliament House in Dhaka was designed by this American architect.
clues.hint: He also designed the Salk Institute.

clues.q: This Sri Lankan architect is celebrated as a pioneer of “tropical modernism.”
clues.hint: His garden estate Lunuganga is near Bentota.

questions.q: Mas huni, a Maldivian breakfast dish, mixes grated coconut, onion and chili with which fish?
The classical dance-drama Kathakali comes from which Indian state?
Which animal, holding a sword, appears on the flag of Sri Lanka?
Which northern Afghan city is home to the famous Blue Mosque?
What flowering shrub is Nepal’s national flower?

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: Built in the 15th century under Khan Jahan Ali, this brick mosque in the UNESCO-listed town of Bagerhat, Bangladesh, is named for a number of domes, though it actually has more.
rounds.a: What is the Sixty Dome Mosque?
rounds.hint: In Bengali it is called Shat Gombuj Masjid.
